record.original_question: For probability tensors, determine which counts of real critical points can occur among the aEDdeg(S_{n1,...,nd}) critical points.

evidence.quote: Problem 13. Determine the possible numbers of real elements among the aEDdeg(Sn1 ,...,nd ) critical points of a probability tensor.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n_1,\dots,n_d\ge 2$ be integers and set $N=n_1n_2\cdots n_d$. Consider the Segre variety
$$S_{n_1,\dots,n_d}\subset\mathbb{P}^{N-1}$$
of rank-one tensors, parameterizing the classes of nonzero tensors of the form $v_1\otimes v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_d$ with $v_i\in\mathbb{C}^{n_i}$. The affine cone $\widehat{S}_{n_1,\dots,nd}\subset\mathbb{C}^N$ consists of all rank-one tensors (including zero).

The probability simplex of tensors is
$$\Delta=\Bigl\{\,u=(u_{i_1\dots i_d})\in\mathbb{R}^N\;:\;u_{i_1\dots i_d}\ge 0,\ \sum_{i_1,\dots,i_d}u_{i_1\dots i_d}=1\,\Bigr\}.$$
A tensor in $\Delta$ is called a probability tensor.

For a generic complex tensor $u\in\mathbb{C}^N$, the squared-distance function $T\mapsto \sum (T_{i_1\dots i_d}-u_{i_1\dots i_d})^2$ restricted to the smooth locus of $\widehat{S}_{n_1,\dots,n_d}$ has a finite number of complex critical points. This number is called the affine Euclidean distance degree $\mathrm{aEDdeg}(S_{n_1,\dots,n_d})$ and is independent of the generic choice of $u$.

Problem. For a generic probability tensor $u\in\Delta$, determine the set of possible numbers of real critical points among the $\mathrm{aEDdeg}(S_{n_1,\dots,n_d})$ complex critical points of the squared-distance function from $u$ to $\widehat{S}_{n_1,\dots,n_d}$, as $u$ ranges over $\Delta$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a 2023 survey on geometry of tensors. No subsequent work fully classifying the possible counts of real critical points among the affine ED critical points of Segre varieties at probability tensors was located; only partial results on average and total ED degrees of Segre varieties are available.

status_evidence.title: Counting Real Critical Points of the Distance Function
status_evidence.snippet: The average ED degree aEDdeg(X) represents the expected number of real critical points with respect to a probability distribution.
status_evidence.claim: Background: only averaged counts of real critical points are known in general, not the full set of attainable values.
